devon_cust: Hey team — we're seeing a surge of 429s when our workers prefetch context for embeddings. This started after we turned on aggressive prefetching for 64k docs. We're well under our account quota in the console. Any idea?

maya_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal request example + the model you're hitting? Also which region and org id?

devon_cust: Model is rwd3-64k, region eu-west1, org: org_42. Sample curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd3-64k","input":"<very long prefetch payload>","prefetch":true}'``` We do parallel prefetch across 20 workers per user.

maya_support: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) are you fanouting a single user request to multiple model calls? 2) can you share the exact 429 response headers (x-ratelimit-*, retry-after)? Those tell us if it's per-model RPM/TPM, concurrency, or team-level throttle.

devon_cust: Here's one 429 we captured: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167890
retry-after: 8
content-type: application/json``` We expected remaining >0 based on console.

ops-bot: [AUTO] Spike detected on model=rwd3-64k in eu-west1. 1m request rate jumped to 2.3k RPM (baseline 350 RPM). Concurrent inflight requests peaked at 420 ("soft concurrency limit ~256"). Queuing and token-level throttles engaged.

maya_support: The ops-bot indicates a concurrency issue. Preflight/fanout patterns frequently exhaust model concurrency even if overall RPM looks ok. Two immediate mitigations: reduce prefetch parallelism (try 6 workers), enable exponential backoff on 429, and consider prefix caching.

devon_cust: We can throttle workers but this is a product-blocker for our latency budget. Is there a per-model concurrent-request hard cap we hit? We saw "soft concurrency limit ~256" from ops-bot — why does console not surface that?

liam_oncall: Short answer: some model variants have practical concurrency ceilings per shard; the control plane enforces per-model max concurrency and a per-model burst window. Console shows aggregate quota (RPM/TPM) but not transient concurrency headroom. We'll escalate to SRE to check shard pressure and queueing.

maya_support: For repro: please trigger a controlled run — 10s ramp, then steady at your usual prefetch fanout for 5m, capture one request id from a 429 response. Also include request payload sizes. We'll fish traces.

devon_cust: Repro steps we used: 1) launch 20 workers, each does 2 concurrent prefetch calls to rwd3-64k every 200ms for 2m; 2) payload ~60k tokens each; 3) observed 429s after ~60s. Example code snippet: ```for i in range(20): spawn(worker(concurrency=2, pause=0.2))```

sre_escalation: Assigned. Please provide a request-id header from a failed call (x-rw-request-id) and the approximate timestamps. We'll pull kernel-level queuing metrics and check if fallback to a lower-capacity variant happened.

devon_cust: One failed header: x-rw-request-id: rq_8b2f9c3a, timestamp ~ 2025-11-07T14:22:11Z. Also attach a short flame: CPU on our side stayed low.

ops-bot: [AUTO] Fallbacks triggered for org_42: 47 requests rerouted to rwd3-16k-quant during spike.

liam_oncall: That indicates smart routing did fallback, but initial shard queues hit model concurrency cap. SRE will look for throttling thresholds (per-shard concurrency limit and short-term burst window). Maya — please open an internal ticket and paste the investigations below.

maya_support: Created ticket INF-2025-9472 and escalated to infra-sre. In the meantime, short-term recommendations to the customer: 1) cap prefetch parallelism to <=6, 2) implement jittered exponential backoff on 429 with Retry-After, 3) consolidate smaller prefetches into batched requests when possible, 4) use a smaller-context variant for prefetching (rwd3-16k) and only hit rwd3-64k for final scoring.

devon_cust: We'll try the rwd3-16k prefetch + final rwd3-64k scoring pattern and report back. Thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:

liam_oncall: If you still need sustained high concurrency for 64k, we can discuss Dedicated capacity or a reserved shard allocation; that'll avoid soft shard-level throttles. SRE will post findings to INF-2025-9472 when available.

maya_support: Closing this Slack thread for now — tracked in INF-2025-9472. Re-open if the mitigations fail or paste the SRE notes here. :lock:
